notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0010] Money is Decimal end-to-end, never float: Money in ledgerly is Decimal end-to-end with exactly two decimal places; convert inputs with ledgerly.money.to_money and round results with ledgerly.money.round_money instead of converting amounts to float.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Raise BillingError with snake_case codes, not ValueError: Invalid billing input must raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a short snake_case code (e.g. BillingError("invalid_tax_rate", repr(rate_percent))); never raise ValueError/TypeError, since the API layer only maps BillingError to 4xx responses.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool from integer checks: When validating integer arguments, explicitly reject `bool` (e.g. `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(x, int)`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0011] Record state changes in audit log: Every payment state transition must call `audit.record` with a snake_case event name and the payment id/amount, mirroring `payment_authorized`.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0012] Raise BillingError invalid_state for wrong status: Reject operations on models in the wrong status by raising `BillingError("invalid_state", ...)` with a message naming the entity id and current status, as `authorize` does for invoices.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Round all monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Coerce prices with to_money and ZERO Use ledgerly.money.to_money to coerce unit prices and ledgerly.money.ZERO as the sum start value, matching line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with stable codes Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly/errors.py` with the established codes: `invalid_state` for wrong invoice status, `invalid_quantity` for bad quantity, `negative_amount` for negative prices.
texts.at-0004: Exclude bool from integer checks When validating integer arguments, explicitly reject `bool` (e.g. `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(x, int)`.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc from clock Normalize any incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic, rather than assuming tz-awareness.
